module_title: Kinetic Energy, Potential Energy, and Commercial Units
introduction: Mechanical energy exists in two main forms: the energy of motion (Kinetic) and the energy of position or configuration (Potential).

core_concepts.title: Kinetic Energy (KE)
core_concepts.description:
The energy possessed by a body due to its motion. 
Formula: $KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ (where $m$ is mass, $v$ is velocity). 
If you double the velocity, the Kinetic Energy becomes FOUR times ($2^2 = 4$). This is why high-speed car crashes are so destructive.

core_concepts.title: Potential Energy (PE)
core_concepts.description:
The energy possessed by a body due to its position or shape. 
Formula for Gravitational PE: $PE = mgh$ (where $m$ is mass, $g$ is gravity, $h$ is height). 
Examples: Water stored in a dam, a stretched bowstring, a compressed spring.

core_concepts.title: Relation between Kinetic Energy and Momentum
core_concepts.description:
Momentum ($p$) = $m \cdot v$. 
The mathematical relationship is: $KE = \frac{p^2}{2m}$. 
This is a highly tested formula. If momentum is doubled, Kinetic Energy increases by 4 times.

core_concepts.title: Commercial Unit of Electrical Energy
core_concepts.description:
We don't pay our electricity bills in Joules because it's too small a unit. We use the Kilowatt-hour (kWh), commonly known as a 'Unit'. 
$1 \text{ kWh} = 3.6 \times 10^6 \text{ Joules}$. (1000 Watts $\times$ 3600 seconds).

important_entities.name: Law of Conservation of Energy
important_entities.key_fact: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
important_entities.significance: It can only be transformed from one form to another. The total energy of an isolated system remains constant. For a falling body, as PE decreases, KE increases, but the total Mechanical Energy ($PE + KE$) remains exactly the same.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: kWh is a unit of ENERGY, not Power
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because it has 'Kilowatt' in its name, students often tick 'Power'. Remember, Power $\times$ Time = Energy. Hence, kWh measures Electrical Energy.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If a question says momentum increases by 10%, use the square rule for $KE$: $1.1^2 = 1.21$, so $KE$ increases by 21%.

exam_strategy_tips: In physics numericals, always convert mass to 'kg' and velocity to 'm/s' before using the $KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ formula.
